items.title: Audit legacy WordPress routes, templates and frontend dependencies
items.description: Create the initial migration inventory and classify routes/features before implementation.
items.rationale: A bounded inventory prevents accidental loss of URL, content, plugin and SEO behavior.
items.user_value: Creates a safe map for incremental modernization.
acceptance_criteria: Public routes/permalinks are inventoried for the selected scope.

items.title: Define target Vue 3 rendering, routing and migration architecture
items.description: Choose the target frontend structure and rendering/delivery strategy from actual site constraints.
items.rationale: Vue 3 does not by itself decide SPA versus prerender/static/SSR delivery or backend boundaries.
items.user_value: Prevents a fast implementation from creating SEO or deployment regressions.
acceptance_criteria: Route ownership and server/client boundaries are explicit.
Builder can scaffold without inventing architecture.

items.title: Establish minimal Tailwind design tokens and SVG icon contract
items.description: Define only the shared visual primitives needed by the first migration slices.
items.rationale: A small shared contract prevents utility and icon drift without front-loading a huge design system.
items.user_value: Keeps the modernized site visually coherent.
acceptance_criteria: No speculative component library is required.

items.title: Migrate the first representative route as an end-to-end vertical slice
items.description: Use one representative WordPress page to validate the entire migration flow before scaling out.
items.rationale: A real vertical slice falsifies architecture, styling, content and SEO assumptions cheaply.
items.user_value: Produces the first usable modern route and proves the pipeline.
acceptance_criteria: Route passes build/tests and visual/responsive checks.
URL/content/SEO/form contracts in scope are validated.
